                                              II.    BACKGROUND

           The Project was recommended by the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc.

(“ERCOT”) in its Permian Basin Reliability Plan Study Report and addendum (together, the

“Permian Basin Reliability Plan”). 5 The Commission approved the Permian Basin Reliability Plan

on October 5, 2024, in Project No. 55718. 6 In that same project, the Commission issued a second

order on April 24, 2025, approving the 765 kV import paths described in the Permian Basin

Reliability Plan.7

           The Commission-approved 765 kV import paths include Import Path 2, of which the

Project is the eastern segment. 8 As recommended by ERCOT, Import Path 2 comprises five

discrete transmission upgrades, two of which are included in the Application for this Project. 9 On

April 24, 2025, the Commission also issued an order in Docket No. 57441 designating Applicants

as the transmission service providers (“TSPs”) responsible for the construction, ownership, and

operation of the upgrades addressed by the Project. 10 Through issuance of the order in Docket No.

57441, the Commission authorized Applicants to file a CCN application for the Permian Basin

Reliability Plan upgrades included in this Project. 11

             The Permian Basin Reliability Plan stems from House Bill (“H.B.”) 5066, 12 enacted by the

Texas Legislature in 2023. 13 H.B. 5066 directed ERCOT and the Commission to develop a

reliability plan for the Permian Basin region to (1) extend transmission service to areas where

mineral resources have been found; (2) increase available transmission capacity to meet forecasted

load; and (3) provide available infrastructure to reduce interconnection times in areas without

transmission service. 14 Pursuant to this legislative mandate, in December 2023, the Commission

ordered ERCOT to develop a reliability plan for the Permian Basin. 15 From January to July of

2024, ERCOT conducted extensive analysis and obtained substantial review and input from TSPs

and other stakeholders to identify the transmission upgrades necessary to satisfy the statutory

objectives of H.B. 5066. 16 This review culminated in the development of the Permian Basin

Reliability Plan.17

            The Permian Basin Reliability Plan divides the recommended transmission upgrades into

two categories: local transmission upgrades and import path projects. 18 Local transmission

upgrades are needed to interconnect and serve projected load in the Permian Basin once power is

imported into the region. 19 These projects satisfy H.B. 5066’s directives to extend transmission

service to areas where mineral resources have been found and to provide available infrastructure

to reduce interconnection times. 20 Import path projects are needed to transfer power from other

                              V.      PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUES 52

        As discussed above, this section of the Brief addresses all Preliminary Order issues for

which there is record evidence, in accordance with SOAH Order No. 1. 53

        Joint Application

        1. Is the applicant’s joint application to amend their CCNs adequate? Does the joint

            application contain an adequate number of reasonably differentiated alternative

            routes to conduct a proper evaluation? In answering this question, consideration

            must be given to the number of proposed alternatives, the locations of the proposed

            transmission line, and any associated proposed transmission facilities that influence

            the location of the line. Consideration may also be given to the facts and

            circumstances specific to the geographic area under consideration and to any

            analysis and reasoned justification presented for a limited number of alternative

            routes. A limited number of alternative routes is not in itself a sufficient basis for

            finding an application inadequate when the facts and circumstances or a reasoned

            justification demonstrates a reasonable basis for presenting a limited number of

            alternatives. If an adequate number of routes is not presented in the joint application,

            the ALJ must allow the applicants to amend the joint application and to provide

            proper notice to affected landowners; however, if the applicants choose not to amend

            the joint application, then the ALJ may dismiss the case without prejudice.

process incorporated public and agency input. 58 Following the public participation meetings,

           The Permian Basin Reliability Plan stems from House Bill ("H.B.") 5066,12 enacted by the

reliability plan for the Permian Basin region to (1) extend transmission service to areas where

mineral resources have been found; (2) increase available transmission capacity to meet forecasted

load; and (3) provide available infrastructure to reduce interconnection times in areas without

transmission service. 14 Pursuant to this legislative mandate, in December 2023, the Commission

ordered ERCOT to develop a reliability plan for the Permian Basin. 15 From January to July of

2024, ERCOT conducted extensive analysis and obtained substantial review and input from TSPs

and other stakeholders to identify the transmission upgrades necessary to satisfy the statutory

objectives of H.B. 5066.16 This review culminated in the development of the Permian Basin

Reliability Plan. 17

service to areas where mineral resources have been found and to provide available infrastructure
